text:
tia_sales: Heads-up — Aurora Finance trial just hit a spike of 429s on /v1/checkout during the pre-demo warmup. Demo in ~30m. Customer surprised. Error shows in console: "429 Too Many Requests".

jon_eng: Which tenant and request id? Are they behind a single-page-app hammering with parallel tokenization calls?

tia_sales: tenant=aurora-fin, sample req id req_af_22b. They said their QA team ran a script with 60 concurrent tabs.

leah_se: Ok quick triage: likely tenant token-bucket exhausted. Short term options: (A) enable a 30m tenant burst override, (B) route their demo traffic to a low-QPS fallback model with less tokens, or (C) temporarily throttle client side using CloudFront WAF rules. Prefer A for fastest win.

ops_oncall: I can apply a temporary burst. Need explicit approval from eng to avoid unexpected cost. Patch command I will run: `POST /internal/admin/tenants/aurora-fin/actions/burst` body `{ "duration_minutes": 30, "qps": 400 }`. Confirm?

jon_eng: Confirm. Do it and we should also flip their routing policy to prefer europe-west-1 (less load) for the demo. Also I'll attach a minimal client backoff snippet to send to customer.

infra_bot: [autoscaler] cluster-epsilon nodes free=1, avg-latency=120ms, last-deploy=stable@2026-11-20T09:05Z

ops_oncall: Burst applied for 30m. Ticket OPS-1210. Watching ingress logs for req_af_22b.

jon_eng: Logs show repeated gateway 429s then a brief window of success after burst:
```
[INGRESS] 2026-11-20T09:18:01Z tenant=aurora-fin req=req_af_22b route=/v1/checkout status=429 reason=bucket_empty concurrent=62
[INGRESS] 2026-11-20T09:18:02Z tenant=aurora-fin req=req_af_22b route=/v1/checkout status=200 lat_ms=134
```

tia_sales: Demo is back on, customer finished the cart flow. They asked about guaranteed capacity for peak hours and enterprise pricing.

leah_se: Next steps: (1) follow-up call about Reserved QPS / Dedicated (propose two options: 5k QPS commit or 1k QPS + burst buffer), (2) share client retry/backoff snippet and recommended max concurrency=10, (3) offer a short dedicated trial for their peak load test.

eva_security: Also note they asked about cardholder data handling in the flow. I'll open a separate thread for PCI scoping and share the SOC2 report.

jon_eng: Action items for engineering: create a demo-playbook doc with a checklist (client concurrency, model choice, burst request process), add an admin API for one-click demo burst (with audit log), and produce a short runbook for sales to request bursts.

ops_oncall: I'll keep the burst until T+25m then revoke. Leaving OPS-1210 open for follow-up.

tia_sales: Thanks team! Putting a calendar invite for 1:1 post-demo to go over pricing and next steps. :thumbsup:
